brief: Write a blog post for my bakery's website. I'm Ruth Kessler, I run Kessler's Bread on Main Street in Sidney, Ohio. Facts: we switched from commercial yeast to a sourdough starter in January 2025; the starter came from my grandmother's 1962 crock; we lost money for four months because loaves took 20 hours instead of 4; we kept 3 of 11 breads; sales of the country loaf went from 60 to 140 a week by September; a customer named Mr. Albright, who is diabetic, told me his blood sugar handles our sourdough better (I don't want to make medical claims). I want people to come try the country loaf on Saturday mornings. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

Write a short announcement for our church newsletter about the Harvest Potluck. St. Brendan's Catholic Church, Sunday October 26 after the 10:30 Mass, in the parish hall. Bring a dish to share with a card listing ingredients (we have two kids with nut allergies). Father Tom will bless the food. Last year 140 people came and we ran out of plates by noon. The Knights of Columbus are smoking two briskets. Sign up on the sheet in the narthex so we don't get nine pans of green beans again. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

Write a blog post for my small engine repair shop, Dale's Small Engine in Marion, Indiana, about putting your mower away for winter. Facts from me: 80% of the spring repairs I see are gummed carburetors from old gas; ethanol gas goes bad in about 30 days; I tell people to run it dry or use stabilizer and run it 5 minutes; a carb rebuild costs $85-$120 at my shop vs $8 for a bottle of stabilizer; pull the plug wire before touching the blade; I sharpen blades for $12 if they drop them off by November 15. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

Write a blog post for my homeschool blog. I'm a dad, Mark, teaching my 11-year-old daughter Anna math through carpentry. We built a 4x8 chicken coop last spring; she figured the rafter angle with a speed square and got it wrong the first time (cut two rafters 3 inches short, $14 of lumber wasted); fractions finally clicked when she read a tape measure to 1/16; we spent about $310 on materials; the hens laid their first egg June 3. I want other homeschool parents to try one building project this winter. Write it now, don't ask me questions.
